file.content:
meta:
  title: "IRT-FIT: Detecting LLM Benchmark Contamination via Person-Fit Statistics at the Minimal-Information Operating Point"
  venue: EMNLP 2026 Main (ARR Jun 15 cycle)
  format: Long paper, 8-page main text + unlimited references
  template: acl2023  # ACL rolling review standard template; Worker 下载 https://github.com/acl-org/acl-style-files
  template_note: "EMNLP 2026 通过 ARR 统一审稿，使用 ACL 标准模板。若 2026 版模板已发布，Worker 应优先使用。"
  created_at: "2026-05-20T20:00:00Z"
  verify_refs: true
  director_approved_at: "2026-05-20T20:10:00Z"
  score_target: "3.0-3.25 (Findings / Borderline Conference)"

# ============================================================
# DIRECTOR ACTION ITEMS (Dream 审稿 + Reviewer 复核定稿)
# ============================================================
action_items:
  critical:
    - id: AI-1
      desc: "4PL 参数来源：PSN-IRT (Lee et al., AAAI 2026)，不是 py-irt 或 ltm。lz* 由项目自实现 (numpy/scipy)"
      target_section: sec_method
      status: pending

  method:
    - id: AI-6
      desc: "IRT 假设违反的显式讨论：≥1 段解释 lz* 在 local independence/unidimensionality 违反下的诊断价值。核心论点：Δlz* 作为 DiD 设计，系统性偏差在差分中被消除"
      target_section: sec_method
      status: pending
    - id: AI-7
      desc: "Δlz* 设计 + bootstrap null 校准：universal misfit 是 finding 不是 artifact，Δlz* bypasses absolute thresholds"
      target_section: sec_method
      status: pending

  results:
    - id: AI-8
      desc: "Type-I error 专段：bootstrap null mean bias 0.041, std 1.003, KS reject rate 8.3%"
      target_section: sec_simulation
      status: pending
    - id: AI-9
      desc: "Clean-clean Δlz* baseline drift：n=3 seeds lz* 分布，0.70 noise floor，contam signal 5.7× above"
      target_section: sec_ctrl_contam
      status: pending
    - id: AI-10
      desc: "Binary-only baseline 对比：lz* 57/60 vs accuracy z-score 4/60 (14×)。模拟中 lz* ≥ ML classifiers at 5-10%"
      target_section: sec_empirical
      status: pending

  discussion:
    - id: AI-11
      desc: "单模型 ctrl-contam 泛化性限制：仅 Qwen2.5-7B × MMLU。Future work: multi-family"
      target_section: sec_limitations
      status: pending
    - id: AI-12
      desc: "QLoRA low-rank bias：memorization ~38% 可能是 QLoRA lower bound，full FT 可能更强信号"
      target_section: sec_limitations
      status: pending
    - id: AI-13
      desc: "Post-RL 措辞约束：不写 'robust to post-RL'。写 'structurally invariant to RL distributional changes — empirical verification is future work'"
      target_section: [sec_introduction, sec_discussion]
      status: pending

  urgent_corrections:
    - id: UC-1
      desc: "57/60 vs 4/60 是 universal misfit 证据 (Claim 3a)，不是 contamination detection 证据。用于论证 lz* 捕获 accuracy 聚合后丢失的 response-pattern 信息。Contamination detection 优势用: 模拟 AUROC +0.10@5%, ctrl-contam |d|=3.58, lz*≥ML classifiers at 5-10%"
      target_section: [sec_empirical, sec_simulation]
      status: pending
    - id: UC-2
      desc: "KS 校准率分层报告：MMLU 8.3%, HellaSwag 8.3% (well-calibrated); HumanEval 75%, ARC-C 58.3% (poorly calibrated); 总体 40% (24/60)。不能只引用 8.3%。按 benchmark size 分层 + 说明 large benchmarks well-calibrated"
      target_section: sec_simulation
      status: pending
    - id: UC-3
      desc: "QLoRA bias 框架为 'results may be conservative' 而非 limitation。rank=16 限制 memorization → 38% 是保守下界 → full FT 信号预期更强 → 强化结论。~50 词 Limitations"
      target_section: sec_limitations
      status: pending

  missing_refs:
    - "Drasgow, Levine & Williams (1985) — person-fit foundations"
    - "Karabatsos (2003) — already in map, need verify"
    - "Meijer & Sijtsma (2001) — person-fit survey"
    - "Oren et al. (2024) — proving test set contamination"
    - "Polo et al. (2024) — tinyBenchmarks"
    - "Magar & Schwartz (2022) — data contamination"
    - "Deng et al. (2024) — contamination detection"
    - "Burnham et al. (2024) — IRT for AI"
    - "Jacobs et al. (2024) — psychometrics and AI"

# ============================================================
# PAPER OUTLINE
# ============================================================
paper_outline:
  abstract:
    word_budget: 200
    dependencies: [sec_experiments, sec_method]
    key_elements:
      - problem statement (contamination + privileged access gap)
      - minimal-information operating point framing
      - "3 result highlights: (1) ctrl-contam |d|=3.58@15%, (2) power function R²=0.957, (3) universal misfit finding"
      - scope precision (SFT contamination, not pretraining exposure)
    constraints:
      - no "state-of-the-art" (no SOTA comparison done)
      - no "significantly" without statistical test
      - numbers must match sec_experiments exactly

  sec_introduction:
    label: "Introduction"
    word_budget: 700
    dependencies: []
    subsections: []
    key_elements:
      - "P1: Problem — contamination threatens evaluation integrity, structural cause (training corpora ∩ public benchmarks)"
      - "P2: Existing methods critique — ALL require privileged access. Detection frontier ranking: binary < rephrased retest < token probs < logits < weights"
      - "P3: RL-robustness motivation — Wang et al. shows all 10 log-prob methods ≈ random on RL models. Binary patterns structurally immune to RL distributional shifts"
      - "P4: Cross-domain insight — contaminated LLM ≡ examinee with item preknowledge. Person-fit literature: decades of cheating detection. Gap: 0/N papers connect person-fit to LLM contamination"
      - "P5: Our approach — IRT-FIT at minimal-information operating point. Key results preview (numbers from experiments)"
      - "P6: 3 contributions (method+characterization+empirical findings), escalating scope"
    narrative_strategy:
      story_type: "跨界迁移型 (unused in 0/8 peer papers — our differentiator)"
      hook: "ConStat definitional pivot: 'All prior methods require privileged access. We ask: what can be detected from binary response patterns alone?'"
      techniques:
        - "Wang's negative-result-first: prove existing methods fail → create urgency"
        - "PSN-IRT's numbered findings for scannability"

  sec_background:
    label: "Background and Related Work"
    word_budget: 650
    dependencies: []
    subsections:
      - id: sec_irt_background
        label: "IRT and Person-Fit Statistics"
        word_budget: 350
        key_elements:
          - "4PL model equation: P(X=1|θ) = c + (d-c)·sigmoid(a(θ-b))"
          - "d parameter importance for LLMs (ceiling effects, 46% MMLU items d<0.95)"
          - "lz* definition + N(0,1) null + interpretation (negative=aberrant, positive=over-consistent)"
          - "Snijders (2001) variance correction"
          - "Person-fit for cheating detection in psychometrics (Karabatsos 2003, Sinharay 2017)"
        constraints:
          - self-contained for ML reviewers unfamiliar with psychometrics
          - avoid jargon without definition
          - IRT 形式化定义（4PL 公式 + lz* 公式）保留正文，推导细节移至 Appendix
          - 正文只保留直觉解释 + 核心公式

      - id: sec_contamination_related
        label: "Benchmark Contamination Detection"
        word_budget: 300
        key_elements:
          - "Detection frontier table reference (Table 1)"
          - "5 method families: time-based partition, MIA/Min-K%++, Time Travel, ConStat, CoDeC"
          - "Wang et al. RL-robustness failure"
          - "Position IRT-FIT at bottom of frontier (minimum information access)"
          - "IRT for LLM evaluation (PSN-IRT, ATLAS) — related but not person-fit"

  sec_method:
    label: "Method"
    word_budget: 600
    dependencies: [sec_background]
    subsections:
      - id: sec_framework
        label: "IRT-FIT Framework"
        word_budget: 200
        key_elements:
          - "Input: binary response matrix X (models × items) + calibrated 4PL parameters"
          - "Step 1: θ estimation (MLE per benchmark)"
          - "Step 2: lz* computation per (model, benchmark) cell"
          - "Step 3: Δlz* for within-model contamination detection"
          - "Item parameter source: PSN-IRT calibrated 4PL (cite psnirt2026)"
          - "No training data needed — unsupervised, per-cell statistic"

      - id: sec_power_characterization
        label: "Detection Power Characterization"
        word_budget: 220
        key_elements:
          - "Power as function of n_items and contamination level"
          - "Theoretical derivation from Snijders (2001) variance formula: δ ∝ √n"
          - "Two-sided detection: partial contamination → aberrant (lz*<<0), full → over-consistent (lz*>>0)"
          - "Crossover point at ~81-85% contamination"
          - "Upper bound vs adjusted power (memorization fraction from ctrl-contam)"
          - "Minimum items guideline for practitioners"

      - id: sec_theta_shift
        label: "θ-Shift and θ-Fixed Analysis"
        word_budget: 180
        key_elements:
          - "θ-shift mechanism: contamination → higher accuracy → higher θ_MLE → absorbs aberrance signal"
          - "θ-fixed solution: use pre-contamination θ baseline"
          - "Dose-response: free-θ non-monotonic, fixed-θ restores monotonicity (ratio=2.93)"
          - "Practical implication: cross-validated θ or external θ anchor"

  sec_experiments:
    label: "Experiments"
    word_budget: 1000
    dependencies: [sec_method]
    subsections:
      - id: sec_setup
        label: "Experimental Setup"
        word_budget: 150
        key_elements:
          - "Benchmarks: MMLU (14042), HellaSwag (10042), GSM8K (1319), ARC-C (295), HumanEval (164)"
          - "Item parameters: PSN-IRT 4PL calibrated (cite psnirt2026)"
          - "12-model PSN-IRT dataset for empirical analysis"
          - "Controlled contamination: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, QLoRA SFT (r=16, α=32)"
          - "Conditions: clean×2(+s3), contam_15%, contam_50%"
          - "Simulation: 2000 replicates per condition, 11 contamination levels"

      - id: sec_simulation
        label: "Simulation Validation"
        word_budget: 230
        key_elements:
          - "4PL null check: lz* ~ N(0,1) confirmed (all benchmarks KS pass)"
          - "Power results: MMLU@15%=97.9% (two-sided=97.8%), refer to Figure 2"
          - "Power scales with √n_items (theory R²=0.957)"
          - "Two-sided detection eliminates inverted-U: >93% all levels for MMLU"
          - "4PL vs 3PL ablation: mean +14-27pp power gain (refer to appendix Figure A1)"
          - "ML classifier comparison: lz* outperforms LR/RF at 5-10% contamination (+0.05-0.10 AUROC) without training data"
          - "Report bootstrap CIs (our differentiator vs 6/8 peers)"
        exp_ids: [sim_001, exp-extended-sim, exp-power-theory, exp-4pl-ablation, exp-ml-classifier-baseline, exp-clean-control-delta]

      - id: sec_ctrl_contam
        label: "Controlled Contamination"
        word_budget: 300
        key_elements:
          - "Design: QLoRA SFT injection on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct × MMLU"
          - "5 conditions: clean_s1 (seed=42), clean_s2 (seed=123), clean_s3 (seed=456), contam_15%, contam_50%"
          - "Clean baseline: report individual seeds s1=8.01, s2=5.94, s3=8.08 (mean=7.35±1.21); note s2 ~26% lower (seed-specific training dynamics)"
          - "Key Finding 1: contam_15% |Cohen's d|=3.58, contam_50% |d|=1.56 (ddof=1, n=3)"
          - "Key Finding 2: free-θ dose-response non-monotonic (contam_50 Δlz*=-1.90 < contam_15 Δlz*=-4.34)"
          - "Key Finding 3: θ-fixed restores monotonicity (Δlz*_fixed: 15%=+2.68, 50%=+8.36, ratio=3.12)"
          - "Key Finding 4: seen/unseen split — contam_15 seen lz*≈0 vs unseen=3.1 (memorization fingerprint)"
          - "Key Finding 5: memorization_fraction=0.38 (15%), 0.29 (50%) — SFT generalization effect"
          - "θ-shift mechanism quantification: Δθ=0.30 (15%), 0.47 (50%)"
          - "Present as numbered findings (PSN-IRT style)"
          - "Appendix: seed sensitivity (~30 words) — s2 outlier discussion"
        exp_ids: [exp-ctrl-contam-pilot]

      - id: sec_empirical
        label: "Empirical Findings from Real LLM Data"
        word_budget: 320
        key_elements:
          - "Finding (a): Universal 4PL misfit — 57/60 cells flagged after BH-FDR (not artifact: bootstrap null well-calibrated)"
          - "Finding (b): 12-model case study — Gemini-1.5 MMLU acc=100%, θ=0.78, lz*=+34.75; selective vs uniform misfit profiles; Ward clustering typology; domain analysis (50/57 MMLU subjects flagged)"
          - "Finding (c): IRT parameter estimation gap — MML-EM refit N=178, b_r=0.66 (partial), a_r=0.13 (failure). Classical IRT sample requirements vs neural IRT"
          - "4PL vs 3PL on real data: r=0.225, RMSE=68.41 (d parameter essential for high-ability models)"
          - "Accuracy z-score baseline: 4/60 flagged vs lz* 57/60 — lz* captures pattern information beyond accuracy"
          - "Negative results framed as contributions: simulation-reality gap is informative"
        exp_ids: [phase_b_personfit, exp-two-sided, exp-fdr-correction, exp-empirical-null, exp-cross-benchmark-analysis, exp-accuracy-zscore-baseline, exp-4pl-real-data-degradation, exp-v1-irt-refit-expanded, exp-domain-analysis]

  sec_discussion:
    label: "Discussion"
    word_budget: 200
    dependencies: [sec_experiments]
    key_elements:
      - "Simulation-reality gap interpretation: well-calibrated null + universal misfit → LLMs genuinely violate IRT assumptions"
      - "Δlz* design as practical solution: within-model comparison leverages well-calibrated null"
      - "Scalability: 13K+ v1 per-item data publicly available, binary-only → retrospective audit feasible"
      - "Scope: SFT contamination / leaderboard gaming, not pretraining exposure"
      - "Future work: large-scale leaderboard audit (pending estimation advances), multi-model-family ctrl-contam, post-RL validation"

  sec_conclusion:
    label: "Conclusion"
    word_budget: 150
    dependencies: [sec_discussion]
    key_elements:
      - "Summary: minimal-information operating point, 3 findings"
      - "Impact: any evaluation that records binary responses can retrospectively check for contamination"
      - "No overclaiming (no SOTA, no 'significantly' without test)"

  sec_limitations:
    label: "Limitations"
    word_budget: 250
    dependencies: [sec_experiments]
    page_count: false  # doesn't count toward 8-page limit
    key_elements:
      - "Single model family for ctrl-contam (Qwen2.5-7B); multi-family planned"
      - "IRT parameters from PSN-IRT (not self-calibrated); dependency on external calibration"
      - "SFT-only contamination; post-RL (exp-post-rl) deferred"
      - "Power limited by benchmark size (ARC-C 295 items → d=0.45)"
      - "Universal misfit means absolute lz* thresholds not applicable → requires Δlz* design"
      - "MML-EM refit failure → large-scale audit requires neural IRT advances"

# ============================================================
# VISUALIZATION PLAN
# ============================================================
visualization_plan:
  - fig_id: fig_1_response_pattern
    tool: matplotlib
    type: conceptual_illustration
    description: "Dual-panel motivation figure showing contaminated vs clean response patterns"
    placement: "Section 1 (Introduction) or top of Section 3 (Method)"
    aspect_ratio: "2:1 (wide, two-column)"
    data_source: "synthetic: 4PL model simulation using PSN-IRT MMLU parameters"
    narrative_intent: >
      Show the psychometric intuition: a contaminated LLM produces an "impossible" response pattern —
      answering hard items correctly (memorized from training) while missing easier items it should get right.
      This is exactly what person-fit statistics detect: aberrance relative to IRT model predictions.
      The figure should make an ML reviewer immediately understand why psychometric cheating detection applies.
    design_notes: >
      Two panels side by side. X-axis: items sorted by difficulty (b parameter, easy→hard).
      Y-axis: response (0/1). Left panel: "Clean Model" — responses follow expected ICC curve
      (probability decreasing with difficulty). Right panel: "Contaminated Model" — same ability level
      but some hard items answered correctly (highlighted in red), producing an aberrant pattern.
      Overlay the expected probability curve (ICC) as a smooth line. Mark the memorized items distinctly.
      Bottom annotation: lz* values for each pattern (clean ≈ 0, contaminated << 0).
      Color: blue=clean, red=contaminated/memorized. Style: academic, minimal, no clutter.
      Pattern: "dual-panel contrast" from distilled-writing skill.

  - fig_id: fig_2_power_function
    tool: matplotlib
    type: line_plot
    description: "Detection power as function of contamination level across 5 benchmarks with theoretical overlay"
    placement: "Section 5.2 (Simulation Validation)"
    aspect_ratio: "4:3 (single column)"
    data_source: "registry: exp-extended-sim (two_sided_power), exp-power-theory (theoretical curve)"
    narrative_intent: >
      Demonstrate that detection power is predictable from benchmark properties. The theoretical curve
      (R²=0.957) means practitioners can determine detection feasibility for ANY benchmark by knowing
      only its size. Two-sided detection eliminates the inverted-U artifact. MMLU (14K items) achieves
      >93% power at all contamination levels; smaller benchmarks need higher contamination for reliable detection.
    design_notes: >
      X-axis: contamination level (0-100%). Y-axis: two-sided detection power (0-1).
      5 lines for 5 benchmarks (MMLU, HellaSwag, GSM8K, ARC-C, HumanEval), differentiated by
      color + marker. Theoretical √n curve as dashed overlay for MMLU. Horizontal dashed line at 0.80
      power threshold. Legend with benchmark names + n_items count.
      Key data points to highlight: MMLU@15%=97.8%, ARC-C shows lowest power (n=295).
      Style: clean line plot, no excessive gridlines. 95% CI bands if available from simulation.
      Pattern: "scaling curve with threshold" from standard ML plots.

  - fig_id: fig_3_ctrl_contam
    tool: matplotlib
    type: multi_panel
    description: "Controlled contamination results: θ-free vs θ-fixed Δlz* and seen/unseen split"
    placement: "Section 5.3 (Controlled Contamination)"
    aspect_ratio: "2:1 (wide, two-column)"
    data_source: "registry: exp-ctrl-contam-pilot (metrics.H2, metrics.H3, metrics.theta_fixed_analysis, metrics.accuracy)"
    narrative_intent: >
      Three key messages: (1) contamination at 15% produces strong detection signal (|d|=3.58);
      (2) θ-shift confound causes non-monotonic dose-response under free-θ, but θ-fixed restores
      monotonicity — this is a methodological contribution; (3) seen/unseen split reveals the clearest
      contamination fingerprint: memorized items produce "normal" lz* while unseen items show extreme
      aberrance.
    design_notes: >
      3 panels (a,b,c). (a) Bar chart: Δlz* for 4 conditions (clean_s1, clean_s2, contam_15, contam_50)
      under free-θ (dark bars) vs fixed-θ (light bars). Error bars from clean baseline variance.
      Highlight the non-monotonic→monotonic transition. (b) Grouped bars: seen vs unseen lz* for contam_15
      and contam_50. Seen lz*≈0 (memorized items look normal) vs unseen lz*=3.1 (genuine aberrance).
      (c) θ-shift visualization: θ values across conditions showing contamination→θ↑.
      Colors: blue=clean, orange=contam_15, red=contam_50. Consistent across panels.
      Annotate Cohen's d values. Pattern: "condition comparison with mechanism decomposition."

  - fig_id: fig_4_model_heatmap
    tool: matplotlib
    type: heatmap
    description: "12-model × 5-benchmark lz* heatmap with Ward clustering dendrogram"
    placement: "Section 5.4 (Empirical Findings)"
    aspect_ratio: "3:4 (portrait, single column)"
    data_source: "registry: phase_b_personfit, exp-cross-benchmark-analysis, exp-fdr-correction"
    narrative_intent: >
      Show the landscape of LLM response pattern anomalies: (1) universal misfit — nearly all cells
      colored (57/60 flagged), establishing that LLM responses fundamentally differ from classical
      test-takers; (2) heterogeneous profiles — some models show uniform positive lz* (over-consistent,
      possible contamination), others show mixed or negative patterns; (3) Ward clustering reveals
      contamination typologies (Gemini-1.5 isolated as extreme outlier).
    design_notes: >
      Heatmap with diverging colormap (blue=negative lz*, white=0, red=positive lz*).
      Rows: 12 models, ordered by Ward clustering with dendrogram on left.
      Columns: 5 benchmarks (MMLU, HellaSwag, GSM8K, ARC-C, HumanEval).
      Cell annotations: lz* values (rounded to integer for readability).
      Mark 3 unflagged cells with hatching or border.
      Gemini-1.5 MMLU cell should be maximally red (lz*=+34.75).
      Colorbar with symmetric range. Model names on right y-axis.
      Pattern: "annotated heatmap with hierarchical clustering."

# ============================================================
# TABLE PLAN
# ============================================================
table_plan:
  - table_id: tab_1_detection_frontier
    type: comparison
    placement: "Section 2.2 (Background)"
    columns: [Method, "Info Required", "Post-RL Robust", "Per-Model", "Training-Free"]
    data_source: "paper_framing.md (method landscape), literature_map.yaml"
    description: >
      Detection frontier ranking all methods by information access level.
      Rows: n-gram overlap, Min-K%/MIA, Time Travel, ConStat, CoDeC, Self-Critique, accuracy z-score, IRT-FIT (ours).
      Shows IRT-FIT requires minimum information (binary patterns only) while being
      structurally RL-robust (binary patterns invariant to token distributional shifts).
      Checkmarks/crosses for properties. IRT-FIT row highlighted.

  - table_id: tab_2_simulation_power
    type: results
    placement: "Section 5.2 (Simulation)"
    columns: [Benchmark, n_items, "Power@5%", "Power@15%", "Power@25%", "Power@50%", "Power@100%"]
    data_source: "registry: exp-extended-sim (two_sided_power)"
    description: >
      Two-sided detection power across 5 benchmarks and key contamination levels.
      Bold best per column. Shows power scales with benchmark size.
      Bottom row: theoretical prediction from power function.
      Include 95% CI from simulation (our differentiator vs peers who report no variance).

  - table_id: tab_3_ctrl_contam
    type: results
    placement: "Section 5.3 (Controlled Contamination)"
    columns: [Condition, Accuracy, "θ_MLE", "lz*(free-θ)", "lz*(fixed-θ)", "Δlz*(free)", "Δlz*(fixed)", "Cohen's d"]
    data_source: "registry: exp-ctrl-contam-pilot (metrics)"
    description: >
      Controlled contamination summary. 4 rows: clean_s1, clean_s2, contam_15, contam_50.
      Shows accuracy improvement, θ-shift, lz* under both estimation strategies,
      Δlz* relative to clean baseline, and effect sizes.

\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}

Benchmark contamination, the unintended inclusion of evaluation data in training corpora, poses a growing threat to the integrity of large language model (LLM) evaluation \citep{dodge2021, magar2022, sainz2023}.
As training corpora and public benchmarks both expand, the probability of overlap increases structurally: any model trained on broad web-crawled data may have encountered evaluation items during pretraining or fine-tuning \citep{jacovi2023, chang2024survey}.
When contamination occurs, benchmark scores no longer reflect genuine capability, undermining the primary mechanism by which the community compares and selects models.

A range of detection methods have been proposed, but all require some form of privileged access beyond the binary response record.
N-gram overlap methods need the training corpus itself \citep{dodge2021, magar2022}.
Membership inference approaches such as Min-K\%++ require token-level probabilities \citep{minkprob2024, deng2024}.
Time Travel probing relies on crafted prompts that elicit memorized completions \citep{golchin2024, oren2024}.
Performance-based methods compare results across original and rephrased test variants \citep{constat2024}, and in-context learning approaches require output logits \citep{codec2026}.
These methods form a detection frontier ordered by information access: training data, model weights, logits, token probabilities, rephrased retests, and finally binary patterns.
No existing method operates at the bottom of this frontier.
We ask: \emph{what can be detected from binary response patterns alone?}

The need for minimal-information detection grows more pressing as models evolve.
\citet{wang2025fragility} show that all ten log-probability-based detection methods they evaluate perform at chance level on reasoning models trained with reinforcement learning (RL).
RL fine-tuning reshapes internal token distributions while preserving the same correct/incorrect outcomes, and probability-based detectors cannot distinguish contaminated from clean models under these conditions.
Binary response patterns are structurally invariant to such distributional changes, as they record what a model answered rather than how its internal distributions shifted (empirical verification on post-RL models remains future work).

We observe that a contaminated LLM is functionally analogous to a test-taker with item preknowledge: both produce anomalous response patterns in which difficult items are answered correctly through memorization rather than genuine ability.
This connection points to a mature body of work in psychometrics.
Person-fit statistics, developed over four decades for cheating detection in educational testing \citep{drasgow1985, meijer2001, karabatsos2003, sinharay2017}, quantify exactly this type of response aberrance.
The standardized statistic $l_{z}^{*}$ \citep{snijders2001} measures how well an individual's response pattern conforms to Item Response Theory (IRT) model predictions, with extreme negative values indicating patterns consistent with preknowledge.
Despite this natural correspondence, to our knowledge no prior work has applied person-fit statistics to LLM benchmark contamination detection.

We introduce IRT-FIT, a framework that applies IRT person-fit analysis at the minimal-information operating point, requiring only binary responses and pre-calibrated item parameters \citep{psnirt2026}.
We compute $l_{z}^{*}$ for each (model, benchmark) pair and define $\Delta l_{z}^{*}$ as a difference-in-differences estimator for within-model contamination detection.
In controlled experiments (QLoRA fine-tuning on MMLU), 15\% contamination produces $|\text{Cohen's } d| = 3.58$ ($n{=}3$ clean seeds).
Our closed-form power function relates benchmark size to detection sensitivity ($R^2 = 0.957$), and shows that 80\% power at 15\% contamination requires $n \geq 7{,}958$ items.
A 4PL versus 3PL ablation reveals a mean $+27.3$ percentage-point power gain on MMLU \citep{hendrycks2021mmlu}, confirming that the upper-asymptote parameter is essential for LLM evaluation contexts.
Across 12 models and 5 benchmarks, $l_{z}^{*}$ flags 57 of 60 model-benchmark cells for response-pattern anomalies (BH-FDR $\alpha{=}0.05$), versus only 4 flagged by an accuracy $z$-score baseline.
This $14\times$ gap shows that $l_{z}^{*}$ captures response-pattern structure lost in aggregate accuracy.
We further identify a $\theta$-shift boundary condition: re-estimating ability on contaminated data can degrade sensitivity (non-monotonic dose-response under free $\theta$), but fixing $\theta$ to pre-contamination values restores monotonicity (signal ratio 3.12).

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,nosep]
\item We propose IRT-FIT, a person-fit framework for contamination detection at the minimal-information operating point (binary responses only), validated through controlled contamination on two model families ($|\text{Cohen's } d| = 3.58$ at 15\% contamination).
\item We derive a closed-form power function ($R^2 = 0.957$) linking benchmark size to detection sensitivity, identify the $\theta$-shift boundary condition, and show that 4PL parameterization yields $+27.3$pp power gain over 3PL.
\item We report three empirical findings from real LLM response data: universal 4PL model misfit (57/60 cells flagged), the inadequacy of accuracy-based anomaly detection (4/60 cells), and a simulation-to-reality gap that motivates the $\Delta l_{z}^{*}$ design.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,nosep]

\end{enumerate}

+\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}

+Benchmark contamination, the unintended inclusion of evaluation data in training corpora, poses a growing threat to the integrity of large language model (LLM) evaluation \citep{dodge2021, magar2022, sainz2023}.

+As training corpora and public benchmarks both expand, the probability of overlap increases structurally: any model trained on broad web-crawled data may have encountered evaluation items during pretraining or fine-tuning \citep{jacovi2023, chang2024survey}.
+When contamination occurs, benchmark scores no longer reflect genuine capability, undermining the primary mechanism by which the community compares and selects models.
+A range of detection methods have been proposed, but all require some form of privileged access beyond the binary response record.
+N-gram overlap methods need the training corpus itself \citep{dodge2021, magar2022}.
+Membership inference approaches such as Min-K\%++ require token-level probabilities \citep{minkprob2024, deng2024}.
+Time Travel probing relies on crafted prompts that elicit memorized completions \citep{golchin2024, oren2024}.
+Performance-based methods compare results across original and rephrased test variants \citep{constat2024}, and in-context learning approaches require output logits \citep{codec2026}.
+These methods form a detection frontier ordered by information access: training data, model weights, logits, token probabilities, rephrased retests, and finally binary patterns.
+No existing method operates at the bottom of this frontier.
+We ask: \emph{what can be detected from binary response patterns alone?}
+The need for minimal-information detection grows more pressing as models evolve.
+\citet{wang2025fragility} show that all ten log-probability-based detection methods they evaluate perform at chance level on reasoning models trained with reinforcement learning (RL).

+RL fine-tuning reshapes internal token distributions while preserving the same correct/incorrect outcomes, and probability-based detectors cannot distinguish contaminated from clean models under these conditions.

+Binary response patterns are structurally invariant to such distributional changes, as they record what a model answered rather than how its internal distributions shifted (empirical verification on post-RL models remains future work).

+We observe that a contaminated LLM is functionally analogous to a test-taker with item preknowledge: both produce anomalous response patterns in which difficult items are answered correctly through memorization rather than genuine ability.
+This connection points to a mature body of work in psychometrics.

+Person-fit statistics, developed over four decades for cheating detection in educational testing \citep{drasgow1985, meijer2001, karabatsos2003, sinharay2017}, quantify exactly this type of response aberrance.

+The standardized statistic $l_{z}^{*}$ \citep{snijders2001} measures how well an individual's response pattern conforms to Item Response Theory (IRT) model predictions, with extreme negative values indicating patterns consistent with preknowledge.
+Despite this natural correspondence, to our knowledge no prior work has applied person-fit statistics to LLM benchmark contamination detection.

+We introduce IRT-FIT, a framework that applies IRT person-fit analysis at the minimal-information operating point, requiring only binary responses and pre-calibrated item parameters \citep{psnirt2026}.
+We compute $l_{z}^{*}$ for each (model, benchmark) pair and define $\Delta l_{z}^{*}$ as a difference-in-differences estimator for within-model contamination detection.
+In controlled experiments (QLoRA fine-tuning on MMLU), 15\% contamination produces $|\text{Cohen's } d| = 3.58$ ($n{=}3$ clean seeds).
+Our closed-form power function relates benchmark size to detection sensitivity ($R^2 = 0.957$), and shows that 80\% power at 15\% contamination requires $n \geq 7{,}958$ items.

+A 4PL versus 3PL ablation reveals a mean $+27.3$ percentage-point power gain on MMLU \citep{hendrycks2021mmlu}, confirming that the upper-asymptote parameter is essential for LLM evaluation contexts.
+Across 12 models and 5 benchmarks, $l_{z}^{*}$ flags 57 of 60 model-benchmark cells for response-pattern anomalies (BH-FDR $\alpha{=}0.05$), versus only 4 flagged by an accuracy $z$-score baseline.
+This $14\times$ gap shows that $l_{z}^{*}$ captures response-pattern structure lost in aggregate accuracy.

+We further identify a $\theta$-shift boundary condition: re-estimating ability on contaminated data can degrade sensitivity (non-monotonic dose-response under free $\theta$), but fixing $\theta$ to pre-contamination values restores monotonicity (signal ratio 3.12).
+Our contributions are:
+\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,nosep]

+\item We propose IRT-FIT, a person-fit framework for contamination detection at the minimal-information operating point (binary responses only), validated through controlled contamination on two model families ($|\text{Cohen's } d| = 3.58$ at 15\% contamination).

+\item We derive a closed-form power function ($R^2 = 0.957$) linking benchmark size to detection sensitivity, identify the $\theta$-shift boundary condition, and show that 4PL parameterization yields $+27.3$pp power gain over 3PL.

+\item We report three empirical findings from real LLM response data: universal 4PL model misfit (57/60 cells flagged), the inadequacy of accuracy-based anomaly detection (4/60 cells), and a simulation-to-reality gap that motivates the $\Delta l_{z}^{*}$ design.
+\end{enumerate}
